items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-02
items.q: Johnny Wiggs, that's where I first met Johnny.

ctx.x: city owned at the time. That comes back to me now. I totally forgot.

And I don't remember anything about it beyond that, except it was a kind of an organizational meeting, much like dozens of other organizational meetings I've been to since. But apparently it took that time, and I remember Myra Menville, Johnny Wiggs, that's where I first met Johnny. Freddie King. Those are about the only people I remember offhand. I remember meetings in the St. Charles Hotel on Sunday afternoons later on, at which there was some music, which was usually not all that great as far as I was…

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-07-31
items.q: when I met Johnny Wiggs and liked him

ctx.x: That must have been the only Boys High.

I think it was, and I think it may have been known as Boys High at that time. I don't think it was Warren Eastern to start off with. No, Johnny, it was a strange thing. At least I took it as strange. Uh, because there were people around doing stuff in music and in jazz, within pretty close radius. But my father, back, I guess around 19, the late 40s or around 1950, when I met Johnny Wiggs and liked him, uh, and I don't remember who said it, I think it was my father who said so, uh, said something, oh, is that…
And, uh, he still lived there until quite recently. He's moved out to the Gatehouse Apartments.

items.title: Bernard Steinau Interview, 1978-08-01
items.q: I don't know if Johnny heard about it from us or, or from whom.

ctx.x: Well, he talked specifically to us at length about that in the record shop, I think. And Greenwood and I were laughing, you know, and I, I don't remember what it said in the interview now. I've got the, you know, the typescript of the interview even, yeah. Well, he got the book almost at hand. But I don't remember that he got that specific, but he...

He got pretty specific. Well, he didn't think it was too clean, anyhow. Yeah, you know, and this was, this was wallpaper that had been on the wall of a building that had been unoccupied for at least 20 or 30 years. Yeah. And, incidentally, well, you, you remember Greenwood and I, uh, got quantities of that wallpaper too. And I think, I don't know, Johnny, I don't know if Johnny heard about it from us or, or from whom.
I think he went with us one day.
